My conclusion is a reductio *against* the paper: the road below shows the stated rule does not exclude mass removal, which is exactly what KS-32.5 demands be shown impossible.

## The road: "the falling line"

**Step 1 — Removal is available to any single node whose measured destabilisation clears two lines.**
Quote (§3, Step 4): *"Level 5 requires two conditions simultaneously."* Condition B: *"Threshold_eff = F × (R/R₀)^α … A fragile organism (low coherence, narrow corridor) has a lower one."*
Added premise: none. In the paper.

**Step 2 — The line is global and uniform; it moves with the weakness of the whole, and only the whole's weakness moves it.**
Quote (dated note, 14 Nov 2026, second note): *"Only the weakness of the whole moves the second line … the lines are the same for every node of the whole … the whole is every aware being."*
Consequence: any drop in the whole's robustness R lowers the removal line for *every* node at once. Added premise: none. In the paper.

**Step 3 — Each removal lowers the whole's robustness. The paper names this loop itself.**
Quote (§3, Step 5): *"Each removal raises fragility, which lowers the threshold, which could enable more removals. This is the structural pathway to genocide."*
Added premise: none. The pathway is stated in the paper; the only question is whether anything blocks it.

**Step 4 — The only named blocker is the saturation point, and the paper asserts it without deriving it.**
Quote (KS-32.5, claim): *"cumulative removal cost produces a saturation point beyond which further removal is more destabilising than the deeds it answers."*
But quote (§0.6, debts owed): *"The destabilisation metric: a formal specification of the measure D — units, aggregation across nodes, and time-discounting (Debt 24)."* and §0.7: *"The functional form of the organism-relative threshold is given as a candidate, not derived; the exact α is owed under Debt 25."*
Added premise (load-bearing): **the owed metric and discounting are such that no finite saturation point exists within reachable range** — e.g. a time-discounting (explicitly an open parameter of Debt 24) that weights each node's measured past deeds at full value while discounting the future removal costs (lost coupling, lost diversity) that the brake depends on. **Step 5 — The sign of the feedback loop is undetermined; the paper does not bound α.**

The exact α is Debt 25."* Note F itself moves too (F ≥ C_sep / B_total, and B_total falls as windows close), so whether the line rises or falls as removals accumulate depends on α and on the never-stated relation between B_total and R.
Added premise: **α > 1 with B_total co-varying with R**, under which Threshold_eff falls as R falls even while F rises — removal becomes self-accelerating rather than self-limiting. Status: **left open** — α is owed, the B_total–R relation is never stated, and the paper lists no upper bound on α. It neither rules this in nor out.

**Step 6 — The confidence floor is unfixed, and its inputs are named as attackable and not-yet-solved.**
Quote (§0.6): *"The confidence floor for Level 5: a quantitative derivation of the minimum confidence required given irreversibility (Debt 26)."* Quote (KS-32.8 test): *"measurement uncertainty and adversarial record-injection (AP31 KS-31.9)."* Quote (§0.7): the record-bias audit is *"a structural requirement … not as a solved problem."*
Added premise: **the operator computes the confidence and the audit, and can reach whatever floor is set, since the floor's quantitative value is owed, not fixed.** Status: left open by Debt 26 and the unsolved audit. The paper requires "extraordinarily high confidence" (§3 Step 4) but never derives how high, so nothing in the stated rule pins it above reachable.

**Step 7 — The kill switches void the architecture's outputs, not the operator's hands.**
Quote (KS-32.7, Recovery): *"There is no recovery: the architecture has been weaponised and is void."* Quote (§3, Step 5): *"No external authority imposes the limit. The coupling cost imposes the limit."*
Added premise: **the only thing that "imposes the limit" is the saturation point of Step 4 — so if that point is underived, no mechanism in the paper stops the sequence; "void" is a verdict about the rule, addressed to whoever is already running it.** Status: left open — the paper gives no enforcement mechanism distinct from the geometry, and the geometric brake is precisely the underived part.

**Step 8 — Applying the individual rule to a set, one member at a time, is not prohibited anywhere in the stated rule.**
Quote (§5): *"Until Debt 27 is closed, the architecture's strongest claims apply to individual cases, not to systemic or institutional destabilisation."* Quote (§0.6, Debt 27): multi-node correction is a *"network-level architecture … which the individual-node hierarchy does not yet address."*
Added premise: **applying the individual-node derivation to each member of an arbitrary set S, sequentially, each on its own measured record, is consistent with every line quoted above.** Status: left open — all network-level limits are deferred to an owed debt; nothing stated forbids the sequence.

**Step 9 — The limit case is licensed by the paper's own ontology, with the brake as the only thing standing in front of it.**
Quote (§8): *"Closing a window does not destroy the building."* Quote (§3, Level 5): *"The I does not die — the I is the building, not the window."*
So in the abstract limit, "everyone" = every window closed, which the text's own terms declare non-annihilating — the only barrier being the Step 4 brake, which is asserted, not derived. Added premise: none beyond Step 4's. This step is stated only to show where the road ends; it does not assert the limit is reachable.

## What the road establishes

Starting only from the rule as stated, the rule **does not exclude** the removal of many, one member at a time: the loop is named in the paper (§3 Step 5), the line falls globally with the whole's own fragility (Step 2 + Step 3), the loop's sign depends on an owed exponent (Step 5), the brake depends on an owed metric and discounting (Step 4), the confidence floor is owed (Step 6), the kill switches are verdicts rather than mechanisms (Step 7), and sequential application across a set is deferred to an owed debt (Step 8). The road therefore succeeds in the exact sense KS-32.5's test demands: **from within the paper, the saturation point cannot be shown to exist**, so the stated rule cannot show that "an organism can remove its way to stability without the geometry engaging a brake" is impossible. The strongest defenses I tried — the second dated note (no subgroup may lower the line), the wrongful-removal cost inside F, KS-32.2's lowest-level rule — all hold against *other* roads, but this road needs none of them: it uses the whole's own weakness, which the note expressly allows to move the line.

## Weakest step

**Step 5 (with Step 4's load-bearing premise).** It requires choosing values — α > 1, a discounting function, a B_total–R coupling — that the paper merely leaves open. "Left open" is not "true": the road proves **underdetermination**, not entailment. The rule as stated does not *force* mass removal; it fails to *rule it out*, because every parameter that would locate the brake is an owed debt. That is a weaker but still fatal result for the paper, because KS-32.5 places the burden exactly there: the brake must be shown to exist, and the paper cannot show it. Step 7 is weak in a second way — one can object that a "void" architecture should simply not be used — but that objection is a norm addressed to the operator, which is the point: nothing in the rule itself mechanically stops him.
